notes:
Written by am-06-x from one page (budget 2-5; the Peru, Rio de la Plata and Peruvian independence pages opened for the sibling dossiers were also read for the 1717/1739 conflict). Not settled:
(1) Dates conflict between pages: the Peru page says the first term lasted 'until 1724' and the restoration was 'permanent in 1740'; the New Granada page gives 5 November 1723 and 20 August 1739. The latter are used in both dossiers.
(2) The page names no extent for 1810-1822: rebel (patriot) land is the Cliopatria 'New Granada' row (1811-1821), the royalist remainder held Quito, Pasto, Popayan, Santa Marta and Panama in practice (not on this page). The 1816-1818 keyframe is therefore only the Spanish Empire shape and needs a gap-filler with the Reconquista pages. Cundinamarca (Cliopatria 1814) is also a patriot row.
(3) Guayaquil 1803 and the Mosquito strip 1803 are confidence 1: the page names no recipient or previous holder. Guayas cells remain in the 1803-1809 keyframe (a keyframe correction cannot subtract cleanly without the Ecuador/Guayas split).
(4) The page lists Venezuelan provinces under 1786-1810 as well as the 1777 separation: the 1777 date is the page's infobox date. Venezuela's own dossier: captaincy-general-of-venezuela (am-06-x).
(5) Counterparts: 'gran-colombia', 'new-granada', 'viceroyalty-of-peru', 'captaincy-general-of-guatemala' (this batch), 'captaincy-general-of-venezuela' (this batch).

Revision of 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review; six more pages opened, so seven in all against a budget of 2-5, because the review found two blocking holes):
(6) Quito: the New Granada page lists 'Quito (1717 to 1723 and 1739 to 1822)', so Ecuador is in the first viceroyalty; the 1717 shape, found and loss events now include it, and the Peru dossier subtracts it (viceroyalty-of-peru_1717, /ledger 1-2). The earlier note ('Quito 1739 to 1822') was a misreading.
(7) Venezuela: the Captaincy General of Venezuela page puts Caracas, Cumana and Margarita under the Audiencia of Santo Domingo and Maracaibo, Guayana and Trinidad under the Bogota audiencia, and calls New Granada's tenure of Venezuela '1739-1777'. So the 1717-1722 shape draws only the Maracaibo and Guayana states, and the Santo Domingo states come in with a 1739-8 gain from the Spanish Empire (confidence 2; the states are the researcher's reading, Cojedes and Portuguesa could be Barinas). The page conflicts with the NG page's own province list (Caracas, Barinas, Guayana, New Andalusia, Maracaibo, Margarita '1786-1810' and Trinidad '1739-1777'): the 1777 separation date is followed.
(8) Royalist keyframes: _1810 (1810-1815), _1819 (1819-1820) and _1821 (1821-1822) are new; _1810 subtracts Cliopatria's patriot rows (New Granada 1811, Cundinamarca 1814, Guayaquil Junta 1812), _1819 is Ecuador without Guayas, Panama, Narino, Cauca and the Caribbean coast, _1821 is Quito and Pasto. New events: 1821 losses of the coast (year only), Cauca (list year) and Panama (20 November 1821; the review's 28 November is the end of the infobox range). The viceroy fled to Cartagena after Boyaca; no page names a capital for 1821-1822 (Quito is the researcher's reading). Cuenca fell on 21 February 1822 and Cartagena in 1821 without a month; both stay undrawn as separate steps.
(9) Mosquito Coast strip: now drawn from 1803 (keyframes _1803 to _1821) and mirrored by captaincy-general-of-guatemala (loss 1803-11); confidence 2. The Mosquito Coast page dates the decree's decision 30 November, the New Granada page 20 November. The strip is a paper claim: the Spanish were expelled in 1800 and never returned. It is carried to 1822 and passes with the dissolve to gran-colombia as a paper claim (identity successors and the dissolve region add it to Gran Colombia's Cliopatria shape, which does not draw it); no page dates its loss or names its heir.
(10) Overlaps removed: Maynas (the 1777 shape now ends in 1801, a 1802 keyframe follows) and Guayas (subtracted from _1803, _1810, _1816). Disagreement kept: the _1816 keyframe still subtracts Cliopatria's patriot New Granada row (1815-1819) although the Spanish reconquest page has Bogota retaken on 6 May 1816 and the last republican stronghold fall at Cuchilla del Tambo on 29 June 1816, so the interior was royalist; the row belongs to group am-08 and should be ended in 1816 there. Infobox area 1778: 2,300,000 km2 against 1,471,878 km2 drawn for 1777-1801 (ratio 1.56): quoted in the _1777 note.
